    Project worksheet

    Last updated on 2026-11-27 | Edit this page

    Use this page on paper or in a plain text document. Write short phrases under the headings; no accounts, software installation, or outside research are needed. The case and service profiles below are the canonical inputs for all episodes.

    Open Methods Kit

    All names, capacities, and service profiles in this case are invented for teaching. They are not claims about real services, prices, or institutions.

    Open Methods Kit publishes twelve openly licensed research-methods lessons and the source for its small website. Readers can reuse the public lessons without accounts. Educators send corrections by email because several do not use code-hosting tools. Two volunteers maintain the collection. Together they can sustain two hours of maintenance each week and $25 per month in service costs. The person who currently publishes updates will leave in six weeks. A second volunteer can edit text but has never published a change. The site works, but there is no documented rule for approving substantial changes or handling a maintainer’s absence.

    Decisions to practice: how to receive a correction; who approves a change that alters a lesson’s meaning; how to publish reliably after the maintainer leaves. The case does not establish what all educators want. Learners must identify one question to ask them.

    Community starter

    Group Evidence from the case Need or barrier to investigate How to ask or involve them
    Educators submitting corrections Some use email and do not use code-hosting tools Can they submit and track a correction? Ask an educator to try draft instructions
    Readers reusing a lesson Public access without an account is required Complete Complete
    Current and incoming maintainers Complete Complete Complete

    Mark one fact and one assumption. Write a question for a named group that could test the assumption. Select one group whose exclusion would change the publishing decision and explain why. A diagram may replace the table if every relationship has a text label and the same evidence and questions appear.

    Support boundary: We will accept ____; defer ____; review work will be done by ____ within ____ (estimate to test).

    Community checkpoint

    Group Evidence Question to investigate Participation route
    Educators Several submit by email Can they track the response? Try draft submission instructions with an educator
    Readers Lessons are public without accounts Can readers find and reuse a corrected version? Ask a reader to locate a correction
    Maintainers Publisher is leaving; second volunteer has not published Can the incoming maintainer publish and recover access? Rehearse publication together

    Tracking responses is an assumed need, not an established fact. Use this checkpoint if you missed the community activity; other evidence-based answers are valid.

    Governance starter

    This is a lesson adaptation informed by ITAV, not an official governance scoring tool.

    Decision Who proposes? Who is consulted, and how can their input affect it? Who decides? Where are the decision and reason recorded? Absence or disagreement rule
    Substantive lesson change Anyone, including by email Complete Complete Complete Complete

    Tradeoff and reason: ____________________

    Backup demonstration: ____; access/recovery check: ____; available time: ____. Conduct-reporting route, responder, and alternative contact (if offering a community policy): ____. Mark unconfirmed commitments.

    Governance checkpoint

    Anyone proposes. The editor asks a lesson user and a maintainer for input; their evidence can change the proposal. A designated content lead decides and records the reason in a public change note, without personal contact details. A trained backup follows the same rule during absence. If evidence is insufficient or disagreement remains, hold the substantive change and review it in one week; continue routine corrections. These are proposed roles, not extra staff already available in the case. The two volunteers must agree who can fill them and arrange training before relying on the backup.

    Fictional service profiles

    These are teaching inputs, not real vendor features or prices. Routine maintenance estimates exclude transition and training work. Treat the case’s time allowance as a shared limit, not an allowance per person.

    Profile Monthly service cost Routine maintenance Publishing and contributions Continuity information
    A: managed publishing $12 About one hour/week Public reading, web editor, corrections by email Content export available; verify handover and account recovery
    B: existing institutional service No direct charge to the project About two hours/week Public reading; institutional accounts publish; outsiders can email corrections Institutional support exists; next year’s eligibility is unconfirmed
    C: self-managed server $8 About six hours/week Flexible access and custom workflows Team handles updates, backups, and recovery; no trained backup

    Infrastructure comparison

    Question A: managed publishing B: institutional service
    Fits money and routine labor limits? Complete Complete
    How will educators submit corrections? Complete Complete
    Remaining capacity and limitation? Complete Complete
    What must be checked before commitment? Complete Complete

    Recurring review/documentation effort: ____ (known or estimate?). One-off transition effort: ____ (known or estimate?). Work deferred or institutional commitment to request: ____.

    Provisional choice: ____ Two supporting case facts: ____ Advantage of the other option: ____ Continuity check and responsible role: ____

    Infrastructure checkpoint

    A is a provisional choice because it leaves some routine capacity for content work and fits the service budget. B saves the fee and offers institutional support but leaves no routine time margin. Test publication, recovery, and usable exports with the incoming maintainer before committing to A. Confirm continuing eligibility and the support scope before committing to B. Neither choice establishes that transition work fits the team’s time allowance.

    Decision record starter

    1. Need and evidence: Educators can submit corrections by email; we still need to ask ____.
    2. Risk, facets, and phase evidence: The impending departure affects ____ because ____. A working website does not establish ____. Recheck this assessment when ____.
    3. Decision rule: For a substantive change, ____ proposes, ____ is consulted, ____ decides, ____ records reasons, and ____ handles absence or disagreement.
    4. Infrastructure: Choose ____ provisionally because ____. Alternative ____ has the advantage ____. Limitation: ____.
    5. Resources and continuity: Recurring labor ____; recurring service cost ____; transition/training work ____; who can cover the handover ____ (or still unknown).
    6. Support and public status: Accept ____; defer ____; review owner ____. Proposed maintenance status ____; release title/version/authors/date/reuse terms ____; preservation location or referral ____; who continues operation and support, if anyone ____. A preserved artifact is not a promise of service.
    7. Next action: Uncertainty ____; action ____; responsible role ____; consult ____; review date or event ____; observation that would make us reconsider ____.

    A justified handover, reduced scope, or responsible sunset can meet this task. Identify effects on users, consultation, and how the status will be communicated. Do not assume an institution has agreed to support the project.

    Review checklist

    For each row, mark demonstrated, needs revision, or not yet addressed. Do not add a numerical total.

    Criterion Status One specific revision if needed
    Need cites case evidence and separates an assumption
    Risk connects facets; phase judgment uses evidence and acknowledges limits
    Rule states consultation, authority, recording, and continuity
    Choice uses constraints, a credible alternative, and a limitation
    Labor, money, and handover are feasible or clearly unresolved
    Support boundary accounts for review and documentation effort
    Citation identifies a release; preservation and operation have separate plans
    Action has an owner, consultation, review point, and reconsideration trigger

    Individual exit

    The publishing maintainer must leave tomorrow. Name the first action you would change, explain why, and identify another facet affected. Write your own response even if you worked in a pair.
